MIDW 101.title: Counselling for Maternity Care Providers
MIDW 101.description: Theory, knowledge, strategies, and skills of person-centered counselling including family systems, trauma theory, theory, grief counselling, motivational interviewing skills, self-awareness and mindfulness, interprofessional communication, and cultural competency in continuity of care. .

MIDW 102.title: Birth and its Meanings
MIDW 102.description: An interdisciplinary study of pregnancy and childbirth drawing on and integrating the disciplines of psychology, sociology, philosophy of science, anthropology, women's studies, and cultural studies. .

MIDW 103.title: Applied Health Services for Maternity Providers
MIDW 103.description: Introduction to diagnostics related to cellular and humoral immune responses in pregnant women and newborns, the properties of viruses, epidemiology, the principles of bacterial pathogenesis, and related physiologic responses.

MIDW 104.title: Lactation and Infant Feeding for Maternity Care Providers
MIDW 104.description: Breastfeeding physiology, pathophysiology, and strategies for support of the dyad based on best-practice principles. Discussion of major Canadian and international initiatives for the support and protection of breastfeeding. .

MIDW 106.title: Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
MIDW 106.description: Covers the anatomy and physiology of conception, fetal growth, pregnancy, labour, birth, transition to extra- uterine life, postpartum and lactation through lectures and lab sessions. Emphasizes anatomy and physiology as related to professional midwifery practice. .

MIDW 107.title: Physical Assessment
MIDW 107.description: Principles of physical and psychological assessment of the mother and neonate. A series of lectures and clinical lab sessions. .

MIDW 108.title: Theoretical Foundations for Midwifery Practice
MIDW 108.description: Scope of practice of a midwife, regulatory framework, skills for basic midwifery practice. A series of lectures and clinical lab sessions. .

MIDW 115.title: Research Methods for Midwives
MIDW 115.description: Research designs used in midwifery research, types of studies reported in the midwifery and health care literature, research methodology and basic principles of epidemiology, biostatistics and social research.

MIDW 120.title: Midwifery and Social Justice
MIDW 120.description: Social justice frameworks and issues as they pertain to individuals' engagement with health care systems. Draws on various disciplines, including sociology, anthropology, gender studies, and cultural studies.

MIDW 125.title: Pharmacology for Maternity Care Providers
MIDW 125.description: An overview of basic concepts in pharmacology, pharmacy, and therapeutics relevant to the practice of midwifery in Canada. .

MIDW 200.title: Midwifery Clinical Care - Antepartum, Postpartum and Newborn
MIDW 200.description: Clinical care of women experiencing normal pregnancy, labour, birth, and puerperium. Clinical education experiences in preventative and therapeutic midwifery care with emphasis on prenatal and postnatal midwifery care. Clinical practice education opportunities within the province. .

MIDW 201.title: Midwifery Theory for Antepartum, Postpartum and Newborn Care
MIDW 201.description: Online situation-based learning tutorials occurring simultaneously with MIDW_V 200 clinical placement. .

MIDW 210.title: Evidence-Informed Midwifery
MIDW 210.description: Principles of evidence-informed midwifery, what counts as evidence? Making sense of the evidence, applying the evidence in practice.

MIDW 215.title: Ethics in Maternity Care
MIDW 215.description: Application of ethical theory in midwifery and health care management.

MIDW 230.title: Midwifery Theory for Primary Care
MIDW 230.description: Care of normal pregnancy, labour, birth, and puerperium with an emphasis on the intrapartum period and assessment and management skills. Includes a four-week intensive session in Vancouver, a series of online tutorials, and simulation and skills lab practice.

MIDW 240.title: Midwifery Clinical Care - Intrapartum and Postpartum
MIDW 240.description: Clinical education experiences with the preventative and therapeutic midwifery care of normal pregnancy, labour, birth, and puerperium with an emphasis on the intrapartum period and assessment and management skills. A clinical practicum in locations around the province. Pass/Fail.

MIDW 305.title: Midwifery Theory for Variations in Primary Care
MIDW 305.description: Theoretical principles of care for pregnancy, birth, and the puerperium with an emphasis on the recognition and management of variations of normal and findings outside of normal. Consists of a one-week intensive time in Vancouver, during which emergency skills certification is acquired, and weekly web-based tutorials.

MIDW 310.title: Primary Research Directed Studies
MIDW 310.description: An original piece of scholarship that builds on knowledge and skills acquired from coursework and in consultation with faculty mentors. This self-directed course can be taken in year 1, 2, or 3 of the Program. .
MIDW 310.prerequisiteText: Exemption from or completion of MIDW_V 115

MIDW 320.title: Midwifery Clinical Care - Variations of Normal
MIDW 320.description: Clinical education experiences with the preventative and therapeutic midwifery care of pregnancy, birth, and the puerperium. Emphasis on the recognition and management of variations of normal and findings outside normal. A 10-week practicum in locations around the province. Pass/Fail.

MIDW 322.title: Midwifery Primary Care Clinical
MIDW 322.description: Clinical course focusing on consolidation of skills and knowledge of all aspects of midwifery care.

MIDW 325.title: Professional Issues in Midwifery
MIDW 325.description: Professional issues in midwifery including responsibilities and conduct, self-care, peer review, interprofessional relations and communication, legal and business concepts, and continuous quality assurance and improvement in practice. A series of lectures and workshops delivered in an intensive format over two weeks. This course is delivered through synchronous and asynchronous online coursework while learners are in distributed clinical placements.

MIDW 326.title: Dialogue and Decisions: Advancing Person-Centred Care
MIDW 326.description: Build knowledge and competencies to navigate complex human interactions around decisions in health care. Flexible, online course for health professional learners. Learning activities include small group, cross-profession discussions, best practice video exemplars, case-based and self-reflection exercises, and a simulation. This course is open to all health professions learners.

MIDW 328.title: Professionalism in Community-based Care
MIDW 328.description: Prepares students for interprofessional and community-based placements. Professionalism and principles of community health and healthcare in rural and remote, Indigenous communities, and global health contexts.

MIDW 350.title: Interprofessional Placement
MIDW 350.description: Opportunities to explore health professions that partner with midwives to care for the childbearing family within the province. Pass/Fail.

MIDW 355.title: Interprofessional Placements in Perinatal Health
MIDW 355.description: Eight weeks of rotation through different interprofessional clinical settings. Students develop inter-professional competencies, working with and learning the roles and scopes of various general practitioners and/or specialists in perinatal care. Pass/Fail.

MIDW 365.title: Community Health Placement
MIDW 365.description: A student-selected, four-week clinical or non-clinical placement in one of 4 settings: global community health, rural and remote community health, Indigenous community health, or a self-selected focus in community health. Pass/Fail.

MIDW 405.title: Theory for Advanced Midwifery Care
MIDW 405.description: Theoretical principles for midwifery care of pregnancy, labour, birth, newborns, and the puerperium. Emphasis on assessment and management skills for abnormal situations. Includes a five-day intensive session in Vancouver, a series of online tutorials, and lab practice.

MIDW 420.title: Midwifery Clinical Care - Abnormal and Unexpected Conditions
MIDW 420.description: Clinical education for midwifery care of pregnancy, birth, and the puerperium with an emphasis on abnormal situations in pregnancy, labour and birth, and in newborns. Clinical practicum around the province. Pass/Fail.

MIDW 435.title: Comprehensive Midwifery Theory and Practice
MIDW 435.description: In-depth review of the theoretical principles and evidence basis for comprehensive midwifery care through tutorials and case reviews.

MIDW 440.title: Clinical Clerkship
MIDW 440.description: Students assume a primary care role in clinical placements in midwifery practices across the provinces. Demonstration of independent decision making and application of the full range of their academic knowledge to professional practice. A practicum under the supervision of a registered midwife. Pass/Fail.
